subject: Post-demo: model fit & acceptance framework for Crescent Labs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara@crescentlabs.com>, Tom Rivera <tom@crescentlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: model fit & acceptance framework for Crescent Labs

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-step plan so we can validate parity against your baseline (BaselinePro v2) without disrupting your production. High-level items: 

- Goal: Determine whether an open-model stack + Redwood serving can match or exceed BaselinePro v2 on your core retail QA tasks while meeting your latency and retention requirements.
- Recommended models to trial (priority order):
  1) redwood/open-7b-v3-quant (fast, low-cost baseline)
  2) LLaMA-3-13B (q4f16) — better long-form coherence on product descriptions
  3) Red-optimized 13B int8 variant (if you need middle ground for throughput/quality)
- Acceptance thresholds (initial proposal):
  - Entity extraction: F1 >= 0.72 (on your labeled subset)
  - Intent classification: Accuracy >= 88%
  - Latency: median inference <= 180ms at 4 concurrent reqs
  - Quality regression: no more than 3% drop in human-rated accuracy vs BaselinePro on sampled prompts

What we propose next:
1) You share a small (2k) de-identified sample and the BaselinePro outputs for those rows.
2) Redwood runs an A/B skeleton: open models vs BaselinePro using the promptset attached and the benchmark harness linked below.
3) We return a short report with per-metric parity calls and recommendations (canary thresholds if you want live traffic gating).

Attachments: eval-promptset-v2.jsonl (prompt bundles + scoring rubric), crescent-sample-schema.csv (sample data format).

If this plan looks good, can you confirm by EOD Monday 1/12 and share an S3 link (or Drive) to the sample? I’ll assign Marissa to lead the bench runs and Ben to coordinate the SRE/latency targets.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

---
Note: if you prefer we can scope a quick PoC with Dedicated capacity for more stable latency measurements; happy to include a pricing sketch in the SOW draft attached later.

From: Sara Khan <sara@crescentlabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom@crescentlabs.com>, procurement@crescentlabs.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & acceptance framework for Crescent Labs

Jonas —

Thanks for the succinct plan. A few clarifying questions before we share data: 

1) BaselinePro v2 — its outputs are internally scored. When you do parity calls, are you comparing to their raw logits or to the post-processed labels? We need method parity.
2) Data retention & access: our security team will need confirmation that any sample we provide will be deleted from any shared runtime and that logs are only used for the trial (no persistent storage).
3) Latency SLOs: 180ms median sounds reasonable. Can you confirm p95 targets and whether that assumes batching?

We will pull a de-identified 2k sample and the BaselinePro outputs. Expect an S3 link by Tue morning (1/13). Procurement included on cc — they’ll want a short SOW and a rough price band for a 4-week proof.

—Sara Khan
Head of ML Ops | Crescent Labs
sara@crescentlabs.com

On a separate note: Tom, can you add the service-level expectations from our infra team so we can avoid re-work?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara@crescentlabs.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & acceptance framework for Crescent Labs

Sara —

Quick technical notes to answer your questions and lock the benchmark plan.

1) Parity methodology: we will compare post-processed labels (the exact fields you rely on in the product) so the comparison is apples-to-apples. We will also compute a logits-level similarity metric but that will be secondary in the acceptance call.

2) Data handling: Redwood will run the bench in an isolated, ephemeral environment. We will not persist raw payloads; artifacts used for analysis (scored outputs + aggregated metrics) will be stored to a tenant-scoped bucket for 30 days and then auto-deleted. If you need a shorter retention window or an HSM/KMS pin, we can include that in the SOW.

3) Latency: proposed p95 <= 420ms under a 4-concurrent request baseline (no batching). If you enable small batching (batch size <= 8) we can expect p95 ~ 350ms for the 13B variants. We’ll measure both with the same load profile so you can pick a configuration.

4) Bench links & artifacts:
- Benchmark harness (unit tests + scoring): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_eval_playbooks
- Acceptance rubric (scoring sheet): attached inside eval-promptset-v2.jsonl (and reproduced in the drive folder).

5) Proposed acceptance gates (short form):
- Gate A (Minimum): open-7b-v3-quant meets entity F1 >= 0.68 and intent accuracy >= 85%.
- Gate B (Target parity): at least one candidate matches or exceeds BaselinePro v2 on F1 + human rated quality within 3%.
- Gate C (Production): selected model demonstrates stable latency p95 <= 420ms and has a canary rollout plan with automatic fallback to BaselinePro if quality degrades > 5% in production sampling.

Attached: eval-promptset-v2.jsonl (prompt bundles + manual rating rubric). Also included a sample SOW template (SOW-draft-jan2026.docx) for procurement to review.

Let me know if Crescent wants us to run the initial bench on Dedicated (we can reserve a small pool for consistent latency). If not, we’ll run on hosted with tenant isolation.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Applied ML | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

[Attachment: eval-promptset-v2.jsonl (prompt bundles + rubric)]

From: Tom Rivera <tom@crescentlabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Khan <sara@crescentlabs.com>, procurement@crescentlabs.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 14:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & acceptance framework for Crescent Labs

Marissa / Jonas —

Appreciate the clarity. A couple of constraints from infra/security before we proceed: 
- We need logs anonymized; request IDs only, no raw customer IDs.
- Retention of any artifacts must be <= 14 days by default. If you need 30 days for debugging we need that spelled out in SOW.

We’ll provide the S3 link (s3://crescent-eval-share/2026-01-sample-2k) by Tue EOD. Procurement wants the SOW and a ballpark cost for a 4-week bench + optional Dedicated reservation. Can you get a draft SOW to procurement by Wed 1/14?

Lastly: one thing we want to stress — BaselinePro v2 includes post-processing heuristics (business rules). For parity we need to evaluate both raw model output quality and the combination of model + post-process. Can Redwood include a simple post-processing shim so we can test model + rules?

—Tom

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara@crescentlabs.com>, Tom Rivera <tom@crescentlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@crescentlabs.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & acceptance framework for Crescent Labs

Sara / Tom —

Thanks — this is actionable. Quick readout of next steps and owners: 

1) Crescent: share S3 link to de-identified 2k sample + BaselinePro outputs (owner: Tom) — due Tue 1/13 EOD (noted).
2) Redwood bench: Marissa will spin the harness and run open-7b-v3-quant and LLaMA-3-13B candidate; bench report due Fri 1/23.
3) Post-process shim: Ben will implement a lightweight shim to mirror the business rules you described; we’ll run model outputs with + without shim for direct comparison.
4) SOW & pricing: Jonas to share SOW draft and cost band for 4-week bench + Dedicated reservation options by Wed 1/14.
5) Security & retention: default retention for bench artifacts set to 14 days; if you prefer 30 days we will note in SOW as an opt-in. Logs delivered will be anonymized request IDs only.

Gating criteria for a canary should Crescent move to production:
- Quality parity gate: no model + shim configuration shows > 3% drop vs BaselinePro on sample human ratings.
- Latency gate: p95 <= 420ms (4 concurrent reqs) for selected config.
- Safety gate: no high-severity misclassification found in a 500-sample manual sweep.

If that captures everything I’ll send the SOW draft and a short timeline.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

[Attachments sent earlier: eval-promptset-v2.jsonl, SOW-draft-jan2026.docx, crescent-sample-schema.csv]
